claims.question: q1
claims.claim: LLMs automate entity and relationship extraction from unstructured text, but they do not store, validate, or reason over that data; that role belongs to the knowledge graph.
claims.quote: LLMs automate entity and relationship extraction from unstructured text, but they do not store, validate, or reason over that data – that is the knowledge graph’s job.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: A production-ready knowledge graph with LLMs requires five stages: data ingestion, LLM-based extraction, entity resolution, graph ingestion with schema validation, and a GraphRAG retrieval layer.
claims.quote: A production-ready knowledge graph with LLMs requires five stages: data ingestion, LLM-based extraction, entity resolution, graph ingestion with schema validation, and a GraphRAG retrieval layer.

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Schema design must happen before ingestion begins; retrofitting a schema at enterprise scale requires full re-extraction and re-ingestion and typically takes months.
claims.quote: Schema design must happen before ingestion begins. Retrofitting a schema at enterprise scale requires full re-extraction and re-ingestion – a remediation effort that typically takes months.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Vector search returns semantically similar text but cannot follow a chain of relationships, enforce access controls, or explain why a result was returned.
claims.quote: Vector search returns semantically similar text; it cannot follow a chain of relationships, enforce access controls, or explain why a result was returned.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: GraphRAG grounds LLM responses in verified, relationship-structured facts rather than statistical patterns, making enterprise AI systems accurate, explainable, and auditable.
claims.quote: GraphRAG grounds LLM responses in verified, relationship-structured facts rather than statistical patterns, making enterprise AI systems accurate, explainable, and auditable.
